subject: Recap + next steps: feasibility to move off OpenAI/Anthropic - compatibility & shortlist
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Novak <claire.novak@brightpath.ai>, Samir Shah <samir@brightpath.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: feasibility to move off OpenAI/Anthropic - compatibility & shortlist

Claire / Samir — thanks for the call today. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and can move to a pilot plan.

What you told us (pain & goals)
- Pain: high and unpredictable per-token spend from current OpenAI + Anthropic usage; frequent throttling during peak billing cycles; concerns about vendor lock-in and lack of ability to pin model versions; compliance team wants tighter data residency and auditability.
- Goals: reduce unit cost by ~30–50% without measurable loss of answer quality; maintain p50 latency <= 350ms on your customer-facing completion endpoints; ability to run sensitive inference in a private VPC for PHI workflows.

Current stack (confirmed)
- Completions + chat: OpenAI (gpt-4 family) primary, Anthropic for safety-sensitive flows.
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small for search/retrieval.
- Orchestration: in-house request router with some prefix caching and an intermediate results store.
- Volume: ~200M tokens/month (production), spikes to ~400M/month during campaigns.

Compatibility constraints you emphasized
- Must keep current request/response schema (conversation + function call hooks).
- Minimize changes to tokenization/stop sequences to preserve downstream heuristics.
- Support for streaming responses and client-side partial updates.
- SSO + SCIM + KMS integration mandatory for any private deployment.

Initial shortlist (what we discussed)
- Llama 3 (13B) family (quantized variants for cost); evaluate 70B only for high-throughput rerank paths.
- Mistral Instruct 13B (instruct-tuned checkpoints).
- A validated 7B–13B instruction-tuned candidate with Redwood-verified safety profiles for constrained contexts (our internal names withheld for the email).

Success criteria (for pilot)
1) Parity on qualitative outputs for 6 representative prompts (you’ll share).
2) <= 1.2x latency compared to current p50 on your side for normal load.
3) ~30–40% lower per-token cost for the same workload profile.
4) SSO/KMS + audit logs available in pilot environment.

Next steps (agreed)
- We (Redwood): produce a compatibility matrix that maps your current API calls to each candidate model/endpoint and list required code changes (3 business days).
- You (BrightPath): share 6 canonical prompts + example telemetry and a 7-day anonymized token usage extract (we flagged usage-export-20260913.csv).
- Proposed pilot: Hosted sandbox -> Dedicated reserved pool -> Private pilot if compliance pre-reqs satisfied.
- Follow-up meeting: propose Thu 09/17 10:00 PT to review compatibility matrix & pilot scope.

Attachments: redwood-migration-checklist.pdf (first draft) and a short template for the prompt set.

Happy to adjust — I’ll talk to internal folks to prepare cost delta scenarios and an initial runbook.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198
From: Claire Novak <claire.novak@brightpath.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir@brightpath.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 17:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: feasibility to move off OpenAI/Anthropic - compatibility & shortlist

Thanks Rishi — clear summary, appreciate the speed. A couple quick clarifications:
1) Timeline: we want a light pilot in Q4 (target mid-Oct) and an internal checklist for compliance sign-off.
2) Data residency: sensitive PHI must remain in our AWS account (we can provide a VPC and subnets). Can your private deployment run behind our VPC NAT?
3) Canary: we’d like a staged canary that routes 5% of traffic to the new model for 2 weeks before ramping.

I’ll assemble the 6 prompts and ask infra to export the token usage file next 48 hours. Samir — looping you on the timeline.

-Claire
Director, Product — BrightPath Health
claire.novak@brightpath.ai | +1 202-555-0147
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Recap + next steps: feasibility to move off OpenAI/Anthropic - internal notes

Internal — quick qualification notes and asks before we prep the compatibility matrix:
- ACV profile: mid-market health tech; expected ARR if pilot goes well: $420k ARR (annualized). Good opportunity for Dedicated -> Private upsell.
- Risk: compliance gating (PHI) and strict residency. Need Private pilot sooner, but that increases sales cycle.
- Technical risk: heavy use of Anthropic for safety paths; need to ensure our candidate models can implement equivalent safety wrappers.
- Ask Marissa: lead commercial (pricing comp + pilot credit cadence).
- Ask Tessa: pull our private deployment checklist + KMS/HSM integration notes; confirm whether we can deploy into customer VPC NAT to satisfy Claire.
- Ask Monica: coordinate SOC2 + pen test artifact handoff for procurement.

Propose we prepare: 1) a short cost-delta model (hosted vs dedicated vs private), 2) a minimal canary runbook (5% traffic, rollback triggers), 3) a compliance artifact bundle.

—Rishi

- HubSpot deal + scope: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/123456789 (shared).

- Next meeting: Thu 09/17 10:00 PT confirmed? Please accept the invite when you see it.

On the model shortlist, we’ll include objective checklists per candidate (latency, top-k behavior, tokenization differences) in the compatibility matrix deliverable.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the compatibility matrix by EOD Fri.
